subject: Ouroborus cataphractus, the armadillo girdled lizard, biting its tail (Logan's confirmed subject, 2026-10-03)
what_the_eye_sees: Hero at 300 px: a scaled reptile coiled round the finger with its head at about 1 o'clock where the coil closes. The bite still reads: the tail thins down the right side and runs up into the jaws. Everything else reads as it did in attempt 7. The head is a boxy block, and a comb of upright spikes along its crown is the most visible thing on it, so it reads as a dragon or crested serpent head, not a broad, flat lizard head. The limbs still do not show as limbs. At about 11 o'clock there is a pale knob on the top edge with a thin diagonal bar running down and in across the band. At about 8 o'clock there is a small X-shaped strut on the inner edge. Neither has an elbow, a hand or toes, and neither pushes the outer outline out, so at this size they read as rivets, braces or a clasp, not as legs. The girdles are even, square-topped blocks all the way round, so the hide reads as crocodile or dragon armour. A jeweller without the caption would say 'dragon ouroboros ring' or 'snake ring', not 'lizard'. Face at 300 px: still the weaker view, and it fails. Seen from above, the head is a shield or lantern shape tiled with kite plates. It is widest in the middle, has a small peaked ridge and flared skirts on the flanks, and pinches to a notch before the ribbed tail. It does not taper from a broad back to a snout. Left of it, the thin diagonal struts from attempt 7 have become a squared block that ends in two pairs of short forked prongs, one pair on each side. These read as a clevis, a crenellation or a beetle's mouthparts, not as forelegs splayed out with hands gripping the flank. On the right, the tail is a row of even ribs, like a spring or a threaded rod. The view as a whole looks like hardware, or an insect clamped to a ribbed rod. Nobody would name a lizard from these two views. With one block-out attempt left, the limbs and the head plan are the things that must change. Spine and girdle refinement will not save the read without them.

changes.what: Build the four limbs as real limbs, big enough to show in both views. Today they are a thin bar and a small strut in the hero, and a block of short forked prongs in face view. Each limb should run from a rounded shoulder or hip into a thick upper arm or thigh, bend at a clear elbow or knee, and end in a broad hand or foot with splayed toes clamped onto the flank.
changes.where: Forelegs just behind the head (theta about 125-145 deg; 11 o'clock in hero-300, the forked-prong block left of the head in face-300). Hind legs at the hips (theta about 230-250 deg; 8 o'clock in hero-300). Both sides.
changes.by_how_much: Upper arm or thigh 1.4-1.6 mm thick, forearm or shin 1.1-1.2 mm, which is at least 3x today's bars. In plan, splay each limb about 45 deg out from the body and take it at least 1.5 mm past the band's side outline. Bend the elbow or knee 70-100 deg, pointing outward and back, standing 1.0-1.5 mm proud of the side face. Make each hand or foot 4-5 toes, each at least 0.5 mm thick, splayed over a 2.0-2.5 mm span, with the claws curled down onto the side face. Remove the squared block and the forked prongs. Blend each shoulder and hip into the body with a fillet of at least 0.5 mm. Acceptance: in hero-300 a bent foreleg with a visible hand breaks the outer outline next to the head, and a hind leg does the same at about 8 o'clock. In face-300 each side shows an elbow out and a splayed hand, and nobody would call them prongs, a clevis, braces or rivets.

changes.what: Re-cut the head as a flat lizard's wedge: widest at the back and narrowing to the snout. Today it is a shield or lantern, widest in the middle, with a comb of upright spikes along the crown.
changes.where: Lizard head part, theta about 93-125 deg: the plan outline of both flanks, the crown spike comb visible in hero-300, and the flared skirts and peaked ridge visible in face-300.
changes.by_how_much: In plan, taper the flanks in straight lines from about 1.35x the band width at the occipital line (about 120 deg) to 0.45-0.5x at the snout (about 93 deg). The head should be about 1.4x as long as it is wide. Delete the crown spike comb and the flank skirts, and lower the crown by at least 40% so it reads flat. Move the spines to the back edge as 3-4 occipital spines pointing back and outward, breaking the outline by 0.4-0.6 mm. Pinch a neck behind them to about 0.8x the head width. Add a domed eye bulge 0.3-0.4 mm proud of each flank, about 60% of the head length back from the snout. Acceptance: face-300 shows a flat triangular head, broad and spiny at the back, pointed at the snout, with eye bumps on its outline. In hero-300 the head top is flat, with no comb.

changes.what: Grade the girdles and give them spines, and dress the tail as a tail rather than a spring.
changes.where: Girdle tiling from theta 125 deg through the palm to about 78 deg; the tail tip at 78-93 deg.
changes.by_how_much: Round each square girdle top into a loaf with a radius of at least half its height. Raise the trailing-edge spines to 0.4-0.6 mm, pointing tailward. Make the pitch fall visibly from 2.6 mm at the nape to 1.0 mm at the tail. On the last 15 deg of the tail, replace the even ribs with small overlapping scales whose spines are 0.2 mm or less. Acceptance: in hero-300 the outer edge bristles rather than steps, and the scales shrink toward the jaws. In face-300 the tail no longer reads as a spring or a threaded rod.
